GBF Pake NATIVE

A desktop wrapper for Granblue Fantasy. This build is an experiment: the sidebar and wiki live in their own webviews beside the game, not inside Granblue's document. The game itself runs exactly as it does in a browser — nothing here modifies it.

Keyboard shortcuts

All of these are Alt-modified so they cannot shadow Granblue's own keys. They work while the game, the wiki, or this page has focus.

HomeAlt+1
PartyAlt+P
QuestsAlt+2
RaidsAlt+3
Co-opAlt+4
CrewAlt+5
SuppliesAlt+6
InventoryAlt+7
CrateAlt+C
StashAlt+S
ProfileAlt+8
ShopAlt+9
Journey DropsAlt+0
ArcarumAlt+-
Alchemy LabAlt+=
Trial BattlesAlt+[
CasinoAlt+]
GachaAlt+;
Collapse / expand the sidebarAlt+\
Lock / unlock the chat columnAlt+L
Open / close the wikiAlt+W
Reload this pageAlt+R
BackAlt+Left

Things you may not have noticed

  • Drag to scroll. Click and drag anywhere that already scrolls — the game's own pages as well as this sidebar — and it scrolls with the drag, with momentum. A drag never activates the control underneath it.
  • Locked mode. Opening the wiki or this page hides Granblue's chat column (Alt+L does the same by hand) so the panel uses that space instead of squeezing the game.
  • The wiki keeps its place. Close and reopen it and you are on the same page, at the same scroll, because the webview is hidden rather than destroyed. This About page cannot wipe it.
  • Reload flash is gone. Granblue can tear its own page down; the sidebar is a different webview and is not rebuilt.

Limitations, and why

  • With Automatic Resizing on, collapsing the sidebar or growing the window for Wiki/About reloads the game. Changing the game webview's width is a real resize, and Granblue refits itself. Fixed Window Size (Small / Medium / Large) does not reload.
  • macOS and Linux are untested in this experiment. The shipping client is also unverified there.

Granblue is never modified

The app reads the game's layout only where it must, and hides its chat column in locked mode with CSS display only. It never changes the game's settings, its code, or its network traffic.
